summary: R4 closure verification: R4-NEW-MAJ-001 (R-024-06 both-assertion fix) is CLOSED — the risk table mitigation now explicitly names both (a) positive: TF reference IS present AND (b) negative: log file NOT modified; both assertions required. R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (safety — meaningful-content requirement) is CLOSED at the four targeted sites: invariant 2 onboarded-operator-bump bullet, invariant 2 blocked-on-adopter-conflict bullet, §6 024B acceptance row, and R-024-07 mitigation — all now require status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stubs explicitly fail CI. However, the surface scan finds two new issues: (1) §1 item 2 still describes the per-adopter onboarding contract as unconditionally requiring 'scripts/enable-required-check.sh invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under branch-protection-log.md' — the blocked-on-adopter-conflict exception is not acknowledged in §1. Fix-round-4 applied the conditional-log-entry fix to §3 line 73 but NOT to §1 item 2. §1 is presented as a 'each cascade slice satisfies' checklist; a cascade-slice author or Codex executor reading §1 item 2 as their contract summary would believe ALL slices require the log entry. This is the same propagation-gap class that produced R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (correctness) in §3 (MAJ). (2) The 'meaningful content' requirement is specified as 'status field (e.g. (open) / (pending)) AND non-empty description after the prefix slug' — but no column position, no valid-value enumeration, no minimum content length, and no regex or format spec are provided. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh cannot implement the meaningful-content check unambiguously from this spec alone: two valid implementations could disagree on whether a single-character description field or a non-enumerated status value passes. The 024B acceptance criterion tests that 'bare-prefix stubs fail CI' but the spec does not define the boundary between a stub and a legitimate row. D-044 defers the scaffolder operational contract but does not explicitly scope the CI script's check-logic format spec — the plan-doc is supposed to be the normative spec that 024B implements against. If the format spec is reviewer-invented at 024B, the protection against the stub-row bypass (R4-NEW-MAJ-002) is no more machine-enforceable than the pre-fix state (MAJ). The R5 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle) is not met.

findings.title: R4-NEW-MAJ-001 closure verification: R-024-06 risk-table mitigation — both positive + negative assertions present — CLOSED
findings.evidence: §7 R-024-06 mitigation (plan-doc line 208): 'CI enforcement (invariant 2): when cascade-status: blocked-on-adopter-conflict, check-invocation-log-entry.sh (a) verifies the TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference IS present in DISPATCH-NOTE AND (b) actively asserts that docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md was NOT modified in the PR diff (closes the R3 safety bypass — a slice declaring conflict-close while actually invoking the script must fail CI). Both assertions are required; one positive + one negative.' The pre-fix language ('skips log-entry assertion ... verifies the TF reference is present') is gone. The mitigation now names both assertions explicitly and states both are required. Consistent with invariant 2, §5.2, and §6 024B. FIX-ROUND-4.md claim matches. The bypass path — declare blocked-on-adopter-conflict, invoke enable-required-check.sh, commit the log entry, reference the TF, pass CI — is closed because R-024-06 now instructs the CI script to assert log-file unmodified. All four sites (invariant 2, §5.2, §6 024B, R-024-06) are consistent.

findings.title: R4-NEW-MAJ-002 closure verification: meaningful-content requirement for TF rows at all four targeted sites — CLOSED
findings.evidence: Four sites verified: (a) Invariant 2, onboarded-operator-bump bullet (plan-doc line 46): 'STATUS.md MUST contain a row matching the standardised prefix TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug> with meaningful content — at minimum a status field (e.g. (open) / (pending)) AND a non-empty description after the prefix slug. A bare-prefix stub row fails CI.' (b) Invariant 2, blocked-on-adopter-conflict bullet (line 47): 'MUST reference the filed TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> TF in DISPATCH-NOTE matching the standardised prefix with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stub fails CI per the same rule above).' (c) §6 024B acceptance row (line 190): 'for onboarded-operator-bump: requires log entry + target match + TF-024X-renovate-<adopter-slug> STATUS.md row with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description; rejects bare-prefix stubs); for blocked-on-adopter-conflict: requires TF-024X-conflict-<adopter> reference with meaningful content AND asserts log file was NOT modified.' (d) R-024-07 mitigation (line 209): 'as a STATUS.md Tracked-forward items row using exactly the standardised prefix TF-024X-renovate- followed by the adopter's <owner>-<repo> slug, with meaningful content (status field + non-empty description after the slug — bare-prefix stubs fail the CI check per invariant 2).' All four sites are consistent. The pre-fix state (prefix-string containment check only) is gone. FIX-ROUND-4.md claim matches. R4-NEW-MAJ-002 safety bypass — declare onboarded-operator-bump + insert bare-prefix stub row + pass CI — is closed at the spec level.

findings.title: §1 item 2 onboarding-contract summary still describes invocation-log entry as unconditional — blocked-on-adopter-conflict exception not acknowledged; fix-round-4 applied this conditional fix only to §3, not §1
findings.evidence: §1 item 2 (plan-doc line 30): 'Defines a per-adopter onboarding contract that each cascade slice satisfies: (a) caller wrapper PR'd into the adopter repo with SCP federation primitive SHA-pinned per VERSIONING.md (D-036); (b) scripts/enable-required-check.sh invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md; (c) post-bake observation window of ≥1 calendar week before cascade declares the adopter onboarded...' The phrase 'each cascade slice satisfies' followed by unconditional item (b) implies ALL cascade slices produce an invocation-log entry. The blocked-on-adopter-conflict close-state explicitly has no invocation-log entry — CI asserts the log file was NOT modified (invariant 2, §5.2, R-024-06). FIX-ROUND-4.md item 'R4-NEW-MAJ-002 (correctness)' fixed §3 line 73 to make the log-entry claim conditional on cascade-status being onboarded or onboarded-operator-bump and noted 'conflict-close path explicitly noted as no-log-entry.' The fix-round-4 inline-fix summary lists six edits, none of which touch §1. §1 item 2 remains unconditional. This is the same propagation-gap defect class documented in FIX-ROUND-4.md's 'Pattern observation': fix-round-3's conditional fix propagated to invariant 2 + §5.2 + §6 024B but not to R-024-06; fix-round-4's conditional fix propagated to §3 but not to §1. §1 is the WP-level summary of 'what each cascade slice satisfies' — it is the first normative reference a cascade-slice author reads when planning their slice. A Codex executor reading §1 item 2 as the slice contract checklist would add a log entry to a blocked-on-adopter-conflict slice, causing CI to fail (because CI now asserts log NOT modified). The inconsistency creates a direct executor error path: the executor follows §1's checklist, produces a log entry, and the slice fails the CI check that §1 did not warn them about. Fix required: §1 item 2 item (b) should be conditioned on cascade-status being onboarded or onboarded-operator-bump, with a parenthetical noting that blocked-on-adopter-conflict slices do NOT produce a log entry (mirroring the fix applied to §3 at fix-round-4). This is the minimal one-sentence addition.
findings.recommendation: Amend §1 item 2 item (b) to: '(b) scripts/enable-required-check.sh invocation per D-035 with invocation-log entry under docs/reviews/WP-SCP-020/branch-protection-log.md — only when cascade-status is onboarded or onboarded-operator-bump; blocked-on-adopter-conflict slices produce no log entry (CI asserts log-file NOT modified per invariant 2)'. This mirrors the identical fix applied to §3 line 73 at fix-round-4.

findings.title: Meaningful-content requirement for TF rows is not format-specified: no column position, no valid-value enumeration, no minimum content length, no regex — Codex executor cannot implement check-invocation-log-entry.sh unambiguously; the stub-row bypass protection reverts to reviewer-dependent
findings.evidence: The meaningful-content requirement introduced by fix-round-4 is defined across four sites as: 'status field (e.g. (open) / (pending)) AND a non-empty description after the prefix slug.' This defines the INTENT but not the FORMAT in sufficient precision for machine enforcement. Gaps: (1) Column position: STATUS.md rows are markdown table rows. The spec does not state which column contains the 'status field' or which column contains the 'description.' A STATUS.md table with columns [TF-ID | Owner | Due | Notes] requires the implementer to know that 'status field' maps to column 2 and 'description' maps to column 4 — but the plan-doc never defines the STATUS.md table schema for TF rows. (2) Valid-value enumeration: the spec provides examples '(open)' / '(pending)' but does not state whether these are the only valid values, whether any parenthesized string counts, or whether 'open' (without parentheses) passes. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh must invent the validation regex. (3) Non-empty description: 'non-empty' is not defined. A single space, a single character, or a URL are all technically non-empty. The spec does not set a minimum meaningful threshold. (4) The 024B acceptance criterion in §6 states the script 'rejects bare-prefix stubs' but does not define the stub boundary in machine-testable terms — 'a bare-prefix stub row' is described as 'no status field, no Renovate PR URL, no closure evidence' (from R4's original finding) but the plan-doc's fix only requires 'status field + non-empty description,' which a single-character value satisfies. The consequence: two valid Codex executor implementations of check-invocation-log-entry.sh could disagree on whether '| TF-024X-renovate-owner-repo | (open) | x |' passes (non-empty description = 'x') vs. requires a Renovate PR URL. Since the 024B acceptance criterion tests the script against a fixture, and the fixture is also not defined in the plan-doc, the meaningful-content gate is effectively reviewer-defined at 024B time — which means the R4-NEW-MAJ-002 protection regresses from machine-enforceable back toward reviewer-dependent. This matters because: the meaningful-content requirement is the sole machine-enforceable gate against the Threshold A bypass path (declare onboarded-operator-bump + minimal TF row + reviewer credits Threshold A without real Renovate cycle). If the spec is ambiguous, the gate's strength depends on which Codex executor's interpretation the 024B CI script ends up implementing. Fix required: add a format spec or regex to the meaningful-content definition at invariant 2 (and propagate to §6 024B and R-024-07). At minimum: specify the STATUS.md table column assignments for TF rows, specify that the status field must be one of a closed enumeration (open | pending | closed) or match a defined pattern (e.g. parenthesized lowercase alphanumeric), and specify that 'non-empty description' means ≥10 non-whitespace characters or contains a URL-pattern. Alternatively, defer the exact format spec to D-044 (which already ratifies the CI script's operational contract) but add a note in invariant 2 / §6 024B that 'exact column assignments and regex are defined in D-044; this spec defines the intent and minimum floor.'
findings.recommendation: One of two fixes: (A) Minimal: add a parenthetical to the meaningful-content clause in invariant 2 specifying the STATUS.md TF-row format: column assignments (e.g. '| TF-ID | status | description |'), valid status values (open | pending | in-progress | closed), and minimum description content (non-whitespace, ≥1 URL or ≥10 characters). Propagate to §6 024B and R-024-07. OR (B) Deferred: keep the intent spec as-is but add an explicit note in invariant 2 and §6 024B: 'The exact column schema, valid status enumeration, and non-empty-description regex are format-specified in D-044 at slice 024B. check-invocation-log-entry.sh MUST implement against that spec; the plan-doc's meaningful-content clauses define the normative floor that D-044 is required to meet.' Option (B) is acceptable if and only if D-044's scope is explicitly extended in §9 to include the CI script's format spec (currently §9 D-044 describes only the scaffolder's operational contract, not the CI script's check logic).

findings.title: §4 threat model scan: T-024-10 describes blocked-on-adopter-conflict business logic without referencing CI enforcement — acceptable by design
findings.evidence: T-024-10 (plan-doc line 91): 'If the adopter has a pre-existing policy-check workflow, the cascade slice CLOSES on the SCP side with status blocked-on-adopter-conflict per invariant 10 (forward-filed TF owned by the slice author; new sub-slice opens on conflict resolution).' T-024-10 is the threat description, not the mitigation spec. The mitigation for T-024-10 is R-024-06, which is the normative implementation-guidance anchor that fix-round-4 corrected. T-024-10 does not claim to describe CI enforcement — it describes the cascade-closure business logic. No bypass surface created by T-024-10's language. All other §4 threat model rows (T-024-01 through T-024-09) describe non-CI surface or refer to existing D-035 / invariant mitigations. No old/weak language found in §4 beyond the R4-NEW-MAJ-001 site (already verified as fixed).
findings.outcome: No new bypass in §4 threat model rows

findings.title: Scan for other TF-row references lacking meaningful-content requirements — §8 Threshold A TF-close criteria are reviewer-dependent but this is a completeness concern, not a safety/bypass concern at this spec layer
findings.evidence: §8 (plan-doc line 229): 'Adopters who satisfied the per-slice bake via an operator-driven bump (R-024-07 fallback) do NOT count toward Threshold A until a real Renovate cycle has also merged + observed clean.' R-024-07: 'The adopter is not credited toward Threshold A until that TF closes + a real Renovate cycle has merged + observed clean.' Neither §8 nor R-024-07 defines what 'TF closes' means in concrete terms — specifically, neither requires the STATUS.md TF-024X-renovate row to be updated with a Renovate PR URL before Threshold A credit is claimed. A reviewer signing USER-GATE-E would need to manually verify the Renovate PR URL exists in the row. This is a completeness/reviewer-dependence concern but NOT a CI-bypass surface in the sense defined for the safety/bypass lens: the Threshold A gate (USER-GATE-E) is explicitly a human-gate artefact signed by @jrnb2024, not a CI-automated gate. The safety/bypass concern at this layer is CI bypasses — automated enforcement gaps. The Threshold A reviewer-dependence gap is a completeness lens concern. No new CI bypass surface from §8.
findings.outcome: No new CI bypass surface from §8 TF-close criteria; reviewer-dependence noted as completeness concern out of scope for safety lens

findings.title: onboarded path negative-assertion scan: no negative assertion present, but bypass risk on this path is a different class (wrong-target, not absent-log) — no gap
findings.evidence: Invariant 2 onboarded path: 'PR MUST modify branch-protection-log.md AND the modified entry's target repo string MUST match the DISPATCH-NOTE's target.' Both are positive assertions. There is no assertion 'MUST NOT have a TF-024X-conflict reference' or 'MUST NOT have a STATUS.md stub row.' A slice could theoretically declare onboarded AND also file a conflict TF. However: (a) declaring onboarded while the log entry and target match is the success-path — no bypass incentive exists for a malicious actor here (the log entry proves the invocation occurred on the correct target); (b) the conflict TF reference check only fires under blocked-on-adopter-conflict path — no cross-contamination; (c) the bypass risk on the onboarded path is a false-target log entry (wrong target, forged content), mitigated by the target-match check. R4's scan (R4-SCAN-NEGATIVE-ASSERTION-GAP-COMPLETENESS) correctly identified that the onboarded path has no negative assertion to add. No new finding.
findings.outcome: No new bypass on onboarded path's negative-assertion coverage

r5_verdict_rationale: R4's two claimed closures are REAL: (1) R4-NEW-MAJ-001 — R-024-06 now explicitly states both the positive assertion (TF reference IS present) and the negative assertion (log file NOT modified), and states both are required — consistent with invariant 2, §5.2, and §6 024B. (2) R4-NEW-MAJ-002 safety — meaningful-content requirement (status field + non-empty description; bare-prefix stubs fail CI) is present at all four targeted sites: invariant 2 onboarded-operator-bump bullet, invariant 2 blocked-on-adopter-conflict bullet, §6 024B acceptance row, R-024-07 mitigation. However, the surface scan finds two new MAJ findings: (1) R5-NEW-MAJ-001: §1 item 2 describes the per-adopter onboarding contract as unconditionally requiring the invocation-log entry — fix-round-4 applied the conditional fix only to §3; §1 was not updated. §1 is the 'each cascade slice satisfies' checklist; a Codex executor following §1 would add a log entry to a blocked-on-adopter-conflict slice, causing CI to fail (CI now asserts log NOT modified). This is the same propagation-gap class documented in FIX-ROUND-4.md's Pattern observation. (2) R5-NEW-MAJ-002: the meaningful-content requirement ('status field + non-empty description') is not format-specified with enough precision for machine enforcement — no column position, no valid-value enumeration, no minimum content length, no regex. A Codex executor implementing check-invocation-log-entry.sh must invent the format spec. If two executors invent different specs, the stub-row bypass protection strength is implementation-dependent. The R5 fixpoint criterion (0 new CRIT + 0 new MAJ on a complete cycle) is not met.
